- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  4–5 days of cough (mostly dry, some morning sputum), runny nose, sore throat/hoarseness, night sweats/feverishness (no measured temperature), myalgias/joint stiffness, shortness of breath without chest pain; Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension; overweight/obesity  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Not recorded  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented); occasional aspirin (dose/route/frequency not documented); acetaminophen/paracetamol advised for fever/pain (dose not documented)  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Not recorded  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Alcohol ~9 pints/week (primarily on weekends); smokes “a small amount,” currently reducing and using a vaporizer; physical activity and diet not recorded; no other substances recorded

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary and reasoning: Adult male with 4–5 days of upper respiratory symptoms (cough, rhinorrhea, sore throat/hoarseness), systemic features (feverish hot/cold sweats, myalgias), and shortness of breath without chest pain. Brief diarrhea on day 1, now resolved. Past history includes type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and overweight. No vitals or exam available (telephone consult).  
- Working diagnosis: Viral upper respiratory infection/influenza-like illness.  
- DDx support (consistent with transcript and DDx):  
  - Viral URI/influenza-like illness: High likelihood given constellation of acute symptoms and systemic features.  
  - Acute bronchitis (viral > bacterial): Medium likelihood with cough and systemic symptoms; dyspnea present but no focal chest signs documented.  
  - COVID-19: Medium likelihood; symptom overlap; no testing discussed or performed.  
- Considerations: Community-acquired pneumonia cannot be excluded without vitals/auscultation/imaging; risk factors include diabetes and age, though no chest pain and cough mainly dry.  
- Management plan (as documented):  
  - Symptomatic care: Rest, maintain hydration, regular acetaminophen/paracetamol for fever/aches.  
  - Delayed antibiotic prescription: Amoxicillin to start if not improving after 24–48 hours; “one tablet three times a day” provided; dose and route not documented.  
  - Safety-net: Return if not better by next week; seek care sooner if worsening shortness of breath, persistent high fevers, chest pain, or inability to maintain oral intake.  
  - Smoking cessation encouraged; patient using vaporizer to reduce cigarettes.

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Advised rest, fluids, and use of acetaminophen/paracetamol; brief smoking cessation encouragement.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Not recorded  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  Not recorded

- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Not recorded  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Viral upper respiratory infection / Influenza-like illness — High likelihood: Acute 4–5 day course with cough, rhinorrhea, sore throat/hoarseness, feverish sweats, and myalgias fits a self-limited viral syndrome.  
- Acute bronchitis (viral > bacterial) — Medium likelihood: Predominantly dry cough with systemic symptoms and dyspnea without focal chest findings.  
- COVID-19 — Medium likelihood: Symptom complex compatible; no testing performed to confirm or exclude.
